sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: bicycle versus pedestrian direction, bicycle light distances, truck no-zones, motorcycle versus moped passing, moped limits and littering fines
Confusable pairs among the sharing-the-road rules, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A02
A bicycle at night needs a front light seen from 300 feet but a rear red light or reflector seen from only 200 feet. [A02]
Why it matters: group bicycle lighting; difficulty high; confusable front versus rear distance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A02
The bicycle helmet rule covers riders and passengers under 16, while the restraining seat rule covers passengers under 40 pounds or 40 inches. [A02]
Why it matters: group bicycle safety; difficulty high; confusable age limit versus size limit.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians walk on the left facing traffic, which is the opposite of the ride-with-traffic rule for bicyclists. [A03]
Why it matters: group direction of travel; difficulty medium; misconception target.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians make up about 2 of every 5 crash deaths in cities but only about 1 in 10 in rural areas. [A03]
Why it matters: group pedestrian statistics; difficulty medium; confusable city versus rural share.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A04
A truck's front no-zone extends up to 20 feet, but its rear no-zone extends up to 200 feet. [A04]
Why it matters: group no-zones; difficulty high; confusable front versus rear.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A04
To pass a motorcycle you change lanes because it owns its full lane, while to pass a moped you keep at least 2 feet to its left. [A04]
Why it matters: group passing two-wheelers; difficulty high; confusable motorcycle versus moped.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A04
Passing a vehicle towing a trailer may need a half mile of clear road, and braking hard near it risks a jackknife. [A04]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A05
A moped is limited to a motor of 50 cubic centimeters and a top speed of 30 mph, and its operator must be at least 16. [A05]
Why it matters: group moped limits; difficulty high; confusable displacement versus speed versus age.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A05
Motorcycles usually stop faster than cars, but more slowly with a passenger or on poor road surfaces. [A05]
Why it matters: group motorcycle braking; difficulty medium; confusable solo versus loaded.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A06
Moped registration has been required since July 2015, and an owner lacking the certificate of origin may file form MVR-58 instead. [A06]
Why it matters: group moped registration; difficulty medium; dynamic.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-R11 | anchor: A07
A first littering conviction is fined $250 to $1,000, while a repeat within 3 years is fined $500 to $2,000. [A07]
Why it matters: group littering; difficulty high; dynamic; confusable first versus repeat offense.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0097]
